text: Every day, IndiaMART's voice bot VANI sets sail for thousands of sellers, chasing one treasure: a short meeting with a sales executive.

But VANI spoke to every seller the same way. Same voice, same pitch, same script. A busy shop owner on his sixth call heard exactly what a large wholesaler heard. Only eleven and a half percent of answered calls fixed a meeting.
So we gave VANI a crew. Before every call, each seller gets a persona built from their own data. And during the call, VANI changes course the moment the seller does.
Here is how the voyage works.
It starts with the map. One lakh forty nine thousand seller profiles, two lakh sixty nine thousand past calls, and nearly three lakh audited conversations.

From those calls, we mined what actually works. A first call fixes almost four times more meetings than a fourth. A slower pitch wins with small sellers. Every finding carries its sample size and a strength tag.
The persona generator turns that evidence into a persona for every seller. Voice, language, tone and a conversation plan, each with the reason behind it. Nine thousand distinct personas, not one.
Each persona sails with one of six VANI agents on Sarvam, carrying seventeen personal details into the call.

On the call, Sarvam listens. When a seller sounds rushed, annoyed or confused, gets interested, or switches language, a switch tool on Sarvam reads the moment, changes how VANI speaks on the very next turn, and writes it to the switch log.
After the call, the result sails home. Calls that need a human ear go to a review queue, and the team's corrections steer tomorrow's personas.
Replayed on real audited calls, the switch lands on the right turn seventy two percent of the time for frustration and sixty five percent for rush, with zero flip flopping.
One seller, one persona. The right crew member for every call. VANI, built on Sarvam.
